win32.name: list_files
win32.description: List files and folders at a local path.

win32.name: read_file
win32.description: Read a text file, or a Word .docx document, from the computer and return its text.

offset.description: Byte offset for text, character offset for documents; use to continue reading a large file.

win32.name: write_file
win32.description: Create or overwrite a UTF-8 text file. Parent folders are created automatically.

win32.name: edit_file
win32.description: Change part of an existing text file by replacing an exact snippet. Always use this instead of write_file when the file already exists, so the rest of the file is preserved.

old_string.description: The exact text to replace, copied from the file including its indentation.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match.

win32.name: copy_file
win32.description: Copy a file or folder, leaving the original in place. Use this to bring an attached image or document into a project folder.

win32.name: grep_search
win32.description: Search the text inside files for a regular expression and return the matching lines with their file and line number.

path.description: Folder to search. Defaults to the working folder.

win32.name: glob_search
win32.description: Find files by name pattern such as *.html or **/*.css, searching subfolders.

path.description: Folder to search. Defaults to the working folder.

win32.name: make_directory
win32.description: Create a local folder and its parents.

win32.name: delete_file
win32.description: Permanently delete a local file or folder. This cannot be undone, so only use it when the user asked for the item to be removed.

win32.name: move_file
win32.description: Move or rename a local file or folder.

win32.name: extract_archive
win32.description: Extract a ZIP archive into a local destination folder and verify the extracted files.

win32.name: create_archive
win32.description: Put a folder or a file into a new ZIP archive.

source.description: The folder or file to compress.

win32.name: open_folder
win32.description: Open a local folder in File Explorer.

win32.name: open_terminal
win32.description: Open an interactive PowerShell window in a local working folder.

win32.name: web_search
win32.description: Search the web and read the results. Returns titles, links and snippets as text, so use this to answer anything you do not already know: current events, weather, prices, or facts newer than your training data.

win32.name: fetch_url
win32.description: Download one HTTPS page and return its readable text. Use it after web_search when a result looks worth reading in full.

win32.name: verify_image
win32.description: Check that a saved image file is a real photograph or picture, not a placeholder, an icon, or a drawing the model produced itself. Call this after saving an image you were told to download, before reporting the step done.

path.description: Full path to the image file.

minimumWidth.description: Smallest acceptable width in pixels. Defaults to 200.

minimumHeight.description: Smallest acceptable height in pixels. Defaults to 200.

win32.name: http_request
win32.description: Send an HTTP request to an API and get the response body back. Use this for a real API — GET with query parameters, or POST with a JSON body and headers. For reading an ordinary web page as text, use fetch_url instead.

headers.description: Header name to value, for example { "Content-Type": "application/json" }.

body.description: Request body as a string. For JSON, pass the serialised JSON.

win32.name: open_with
win32.description: Open a file in a named program rather than whatever Windows opens it with by default, for example opening an .html file in notepad instead of a browser.

path.description: Full path to the file to open.

program.description: Program name or full path, for example notepad, mspaint, or wordpad.

win32.name: clipboard_write
win32.description: Put text on the Windows clipboard so it can be pasted into another program.

win32.name: clipboard_read
win32.description: Read whatever text is currently on the Windows clipboard. Useful for getting a value out of a program that offers a Copy button but no file export.

win32.name: browser_save_pdf
win32.description: Save the page currently open in the browser as a PDF file. Use this for an invoice, receipt, confirmation or ticket that only exists as a web page.

path.description: Where to save it, ending in .pdf.

win32.name: wait_for_download
win32.description: Wait until a file that a page started downloading has finished arriving, and return its path. Call this straight after clicking a download link, instead of guessing that the file is ready.

folder.description: Folder the download lands in. Defaults to your output folder.

timeoutSeconds.description: Optional user-requested deadline. Omit to wait until complete or stopped.

nameContains.description: Only accept a file whose name contains this text.

win32.name: upload_file
win32.description: Attach a local file to a file-upload control on the current page, the same as choosing it in the file picker. Read the page first to get the id of the upload field.

ref.description: Element id of the file input, from browser_read.

path.description: Full path to the file to attach.

win32.name: get_datetime
win32.description: Get the current date and time. Pass an IANA time zone such as America/New_York or Europe/London to get the time in that place; omit it for this computer's local time.

win32.name: open_search_in_browser
win32.description: Open a Google search in the agent's own browser window for the user to look at. This does not return results to you; use web_search when you need the answer yourself.

win32.name: run_command
win32.description: Run a PowerShell command with full local permissions in the requested working folder.

win32.name: open_url
win32.description: Open an HTTPS URL in the agent's own browser window (a separate profile, never the user's) for the user to see.

win32.name: open_page
win32.description: Open a web page in the agent's own browser window (a separate profile, never the user's) and bring it to the front, so you can then read it, click it, or type into it.

win32.name: browser_read
win32.description: Read the current web page as structured data: its text plus every clickable and typable element with a short id. This is the fast, exact way to see a page. Always prefer it over screenshots for anything in a browser.

win32.name: browser_text
win32.description: Read only the words on the current page, with no clickable element list. Use this when you just need to read an article, a result or a description and are not going to click anything, because it costs a fraction of what browser_read does on a long page.

maxCharacters.description: Stop after this many characters. Defaults to 40000.

win32.name: browser_screenshot
win32.description: Save a picture of the page currently open in the browser. Use this to show someone what a page looks like, or to check a layout. To read a page, use browser_text or browser_read instead — they are faster and exact.

path.description: Where to save it, ending in .png.

win32.name: browser_find
win32.description: Find elements on the current page whose text, label or placeholder contains a phrase. Returns their ids so you can click or fill them.

query.description: Words to look for, for example "Send" or "Search mail".

win32.name: browser_click
win32.description: Click an element on the page by the id browser_read gave it. Exact, no coordinates, no guessing.

win32.name: browser_fill
win32.description: Type an exact value into a text box, textarea or dropdown by its element id.

win32.name: browser_press
win32.description: Press a key such as Enter, Tab or Escape, optionally after focusing an element id.

key.description: Enter, Tab, Escape, ArrowDown, PageDown, and similar.

ref.description: Optional element id to focus first.

win32.name: browser_scroll
win32.description: Scroll the current page by a number of pixels. Positive scrolls down.

delta.description: Pixels to scroll, for example 800 or -800.

win32.name: browser_back
win32.description: Go back to the previous page in this browser tab.

win32.name: browser_wait_for
win32.description: Wait until a phrase appears on the page, for slow pages and apps that load after navigation.

win32.name: browser_tabs
win32.description: List the open browser tabs with their ids, titles and URLs.

win32.name: browser_open_tab
win32.description: Open one HTTPS page in a new browser tab and switch to it. Use this only for a small set of separate items that must be compared, such as the top 3–5 results from a ranked list.

url.description: The complete HTTPS URL to open.

win32.name: browser_switch_tab
win32.description: Switch to one of the open tabs by its id.

win32.name: browser_extensions
win32.description: List the browser extension windows that are currently open — a wallet asking to confirm, a VPN choosing a location, any extension popup — and the extensions installed in this browser. Call this when a task involves an extension, or when a page seems to be waiting on one.

win32.name: browser_focus_extension
win32.description: Switch to an open extension window so you can read and click inside it with the ordinary page tools. Use this to press Confirm, Approve, Sign, Connect or similar inside an extension. Switch back to the page afterwards with browser_switch_tab.

viewId.description: The viewId from browser_extensions. Omit it when only one extension window is open.

win32.name: browser_extract
win32.description: Pull a repeating list off the page as rows of data in one call: search results, table rows, product cards, listings. Give the CSS selector for one repeating item and a map of field name to selector. Add @href or @src to take an attribute instead of the text. Far faster than reading and scrolling.

rowSelector.description: CSS selector matching one repeating item, for example "article.listing" or "table tbody tr".

fields.description: Field name to selector within the row. Example: { "title": "h2", "price": ".price", "link": "a@href" }. Use "" to take the row text itself.

win32.name: browser_wait_for_idle
win32.description: Wait until the page has finished loading and its network traffic has gone quiet. Call this after navigating or clicking something slow, instead of reading the page over and over to see whether it is ready.

quietMillis.description: How long the network must stay quiet. Default 700.

timeoutSeconds.description: Optional user-requested deadline in seconds. Omit to wait until ready or stopped.

win32.name: browser_click_and_wait
win32.description: Click something and wait for what it was meant to cause, in one call: a new page, or some text appearing. Use this instead of clicking and then reading the page repeatedly to see whether it worked.

waitForText.description: Wait until this text appears on the page.

win32.name: browser_fill_form
win32.description: Fill several fields on the page in one call, then optionally press a button. Use this for a login or any form rather than filling one field per call.

fields.description: The fields to fill, in order.

submitRef.description: Element id of the button to click once the fields are filled.

win32.name: browser_evaluate
win32.description: Run a JavaScript expression inside the current page and get its value back. The fastest way to pull structured data out of a page: one call can return every row of a table or every listing on a results page as JSON, instead of reading and scrolling many times. The expression is evaluated in the page, so document, window and querySelectorAll are all available.

resultId.description: Temporary result ID returned by an earlier evaluation; set expression to an empty string when continuing.

offset.description: nextOffset returned by the previous result chunk.

expression.description: A JavaScript expression. Example: [...document.querySelectorAll("article")].map(a => ({ title: a.querySelector("h2")?.innerText, href: a.querySelector("a")?.href }))

win32.name: browser_console
win32.description: Read the browser console for the current page: script errors, warnings and log output. Use this when a page looks broken, half-loaded, or does not respond the way the page text suggests it should.

level.description: Use "error" for only errors and warnings.

limit.description: How many of the most recent messages to return. Default 50.

win32.name: browser_network
win32.description: List the network requests the current page made, with method, URL and status. Use it to find a blocked or failing request, or to spot the underlying data API a page calls, which is often quicker to read than the rendered page.

failedOnly.description: Only requests that failed or returned status 400 or above.

urlPattern.description: Only requests whose URL contains this text.

limit.description: How many of the most recent requests to return. Default 50.

win32.name: browser_hover
win32.description: Move the pointer onto an element without clicking, to open a hover menu or reveal a tooltip. Read the page afterwards to see what appeared.

win32.name: browser_click_special
win32.description: Click an element with the right mouse button, or double-click it. Use this for context menus and for lists where opening an item needs a double click. An ordinary single left click is browser_click.

clickCount.description: Use 2 for a double click. Default 1.

win32.name: browser_drag
win32.description: Drag one element onto another: reordering a list, moving a card between columns, or setting a slider.

fromRef.description: Element id to drag, from browser_read.

toRef.description: Element id to drop it onto, from browser_read.

win32.name: browser_resize
win32.description: Set the size of the page viewport, optionally emulating a mobile device. Useful for checking a mobile layout, and for making a page narrow enough that its content needs less scrolling.

mobile.description: Emulate a touch mobile device at that size.

win32.name: browser_close_tab
win32.description: Close one tab you opened, by its id. Use this to tidy up the extra tabs you opened before you give your final answer. Never close a tab that was already open before you started.

win32.name: read_screen
win32.description: Read the window that is in front — the open web page or app — and return its visible text and the buttons, links and fields you can act on. Call this before clicking or typing so you know what is really there.

win32.name: click_element
win32.description: Click a button, link, checkbox or menu item in the window in front, found by the text you can see on it.

name.description: The visible text of the thing to click, copied from read_screen.

win32.name: type_text
win32.description: Type text into the window in front. Pass into with a field name from read_screen to fill that field, or leave it out to type wherever the cursor already is.

into.description: The name or label of the field to type into.

win32.name: press_key
win32.description: Press one key in the window in front, such as Enter, Tab, Escape, PageDown, or a combination like Ctrl+S.

win32.name: scroll_page
win32.description: Scroll the window in front up or down to bring more content into view.

amount.description: How many notches to scroll. Defaults to 3.

win32.name: take_screenshot
win32.description: Save a PNG picture of the screen to a local file, so the user can see what is on it.

path.description: Where to save the .png file.

win32.name: check_screen
win32.description: Look at the screen and answer one yes/no question about it, for confirming a result you cannot read any other way. Returns a verdict and what was seen. Saves no file.

question.description: One thing to confirm, e.g. "does the calculator show 64".

win32.name: list_windows
win32.description: List the application windows that are open on this computer.

win32.name: focus_window
win32.description: Bring an open window to the front by its title, so read_screen and click_element act on that app.

win32.name: open_app
win32.description: Start a Windows program, such as notepad, calc, or the full path to an .exe.

name.description: The program to start, for example notepad.

win32.name: download_file
win32.description: Download a file from an http(s) URL and save it to a local path. Use this for a real file — a PDF, an image, an archive — not for reading a page as text.

path.description: Where to save it, including the file name and extension.

win32.name: write_document
win32.description: Create a proper Word .docx, .pdf or Excel .xlsx file from content you write. Use this whenever the user asks for a Word document, a PDF, a report, a letter or a spreadsheet. You do not need Microsoft Office; it builds the file itself.

path.description: The output file, ending in .docx, .pdf or .xlsx.

content.description: For .docx and .pdf, the complete body text; start a line with # for a heading or - for a bullet. In a .pdf you can also place a picture you have already downloaded by putting its full path on its own line as ![](C: olderpicture.png) - use that to put each image beside the text about it. For .xlsx, comma-separated rows one per line, header row first.

darwin.description: Read the window that is in front — the open web page or app — and return its visible text and the buttons, links and fields you can act on. Call this before clicking or typing so you know what is really there.

darwin.name: click_element
darwin.description: Click a button, link, checkbox or menu item in the window in front, found by the text you can see on it.

name.description: The visible text of the thing to click, copied from read_screen.

darwin.name: type_text
darwin.description: Type text into the window in front. Pass into with a field name from read_screen to fill that field, or leave it out to type wherever the cursor already is.

into.description: The name or label of the field to type into.

darwin.name: press_key
darwin.description: Press one key in the window in front, such as Enter, Tab, Escape, PageDown, or a combination like Cmd+S.

darwin.name: scroll_page
darwin.description: Scroll the window in front up or down to bring more content into view.

amount.description: How many notches to scroll. Defaults to 3.

darwin.name: take_screenshot
darwin.description: Save a PNG picture of the screen to a local file, so the user can see what is on it.

path.description: Where to save the .png file.

darwin.name: check_screen
darwin.description: Look at the screen and answer one yes/no question about it, for confirming a result you cannot read any other way. Returns a verdict and what was seen. Saves no file.

question.description: One thing to confirm, e.g. "does the calculator show 64".

darwin.name: list_windows
darwin.description: List the application windows that are open on this computer.

darwin.name: focus_window
darwin.description: Bring an open window to the front by its title, so read_screen and click_element act on that app.

darwin.name: open_app
darwin.description: Start a macOS application, such as TextEdit, Calculator, or the full path to an .app.

name.description: The application to start, for example TextEdit.

darwin.name: download_file
darwin.description: Download a file from an http(s) URL and save it to a local path. Use this for a real file — a PDF, an image, an archive — not for reading a page as text.

path.description: Where to save it, including the file name and extension.

darwin.name: write_document
darwin.description: Create a proper Word .docx, .pdf or Excel .xlsx file from content you write. Use this whenever the user asks for a Word document, a PDF, a report, a letter or a spreadsheet. You do not need Microsoft Office; it builds the file itself.

path.description: The output file, ending in .docx, .pdf or .xlsx.

content.description: For .docx and .pdf, the complete body text; start a line with # for a heading or - for a bullet. In a .pdf you can also place a picture you have already downloaded by putting its full path on its own line as ![](C: olderpicture.png) - use that to put each image beside the text about it. For .xlsx, comma-separated rows one per line, header row first.

linux.name: list_files
linux.description: List files and folders at a local path.

linux.name: read_file
linux.description: Read a text file, or a Word .docx document, from the computer and return its text.

offset.description: Byte offset for text, character offset for documents; use to continue reading a large file.

linux.name: write_file
linux.description: Create or overwrite a UTF-8 text file. Parent folders are created automatically.

linux.name: edit_file
linux.description: Change part of an existing text file by replacing an exact snippet. Always use this instead of write_file when the file already exists, so the rest of the file is preserved.

old_string.description: The exact text to replace, copied from the file including its indentation.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match.

linux.name: copy_file
linux.description: Copy a file or folder, leaving the original in place. Use this to bring an attached image or document into a project folder.

linux.name: grep_search
linux.description: Search the text inside files for a regular expression and return the matching lines with their file and line number.

path.description: Folder to search. Defaults to the working folder.

linux.name: glob_search
linux.description: Find files by name pattern such as *.html or **/*.css, searching subfolders.

path.description: Folder to search. Defaults to the working folder.

linux.name: make_directory
linux.description: Create a local folder and its parents.

linux.name: delete_file
linux.description: Permanently delete a local file or folder. This cannot be undone, so only use it when the user asked for the item to be removed.

linux.name: move_file
linux.description: Move or rename a local file or folder.

linux.name: extract_archive
linux.description: Extract a ZIP archive into a local destination folder and verify the extracted files.

linux.name: create_archive
linux.description: Put a folder or a file into a new ZIP archive.

source.description: The folder or file to compress.

linux.name: open_folder
linux.description: Open a local folder in the file manager.

linux.name: open_terminal
linux.description: Open an interactive the terminal window in a local working folder.

linux.name: web_search
linux.description: Search the web and read the results. Returns titles, links and snippets as text, so use this to answer anything you do not already know: current events, weather, prices, or facts newer than your training data.

linux.name: fetch_url
linux.description: Download one HTTPS page and return its readable text. Use it after web_search when a result looks worth reading in full.

linux.name: verify_image
linux.description: Check that a saved image file is a real photograph or picture, not a placeholder, an icon, or a drawing the model produced itself. Call this after saving an image you were told to download, before reporting the step done.

path.description: Full path to the image file.

minimumWidth.description: Smallest acceptable width in pixels. Defaults to 200.

minimumHeight.description: Smallest acceptable height in pixels. Defaults to 200.

linux.name: http_request
linux.description: Send an HTTP request to an API and get the response body back. Use this for a real API — GET with query parameters, or POST with a JSON body and headers. For reading an ordinary web page as text, use fetch_url instead.

headers.description: Header name to value, for example { "Content-Type": "application/json" }.

body.description: Request body as a string. For JSON, pass the serialised JSON.

linux.name: open_with
linux.description: Open a file in a named application rather than whatever Linux opens it with by default, for example opening an .html file in Text Editor instead of a browser.

path.description: Full path to the file to open.

program.description: Application name or full path, for example Text Editor, Image Viewer, or Document Viewer.

linux.name: clipboard_write
linux.description: Put text on the Linux clipboard so it can be pasted into another application.

linux.name: clipboard_read
linux.description: Read whatever text is currently on the Linux clipboard. Useful for getting a value out of a application that offers a Copy button but no file export.

linux.name: browser_save_pdf
linux.description: Save the page currently open in the browser as a PDF file. Use this for an invoice, receipt, confirmation or ticket that only exists as a web page.

path.description: Where to save it, ending in .pdf.

linux.name: wait_for_download
linux.description: Wait until a file that a page started downloading has finished arriving, and return its path. Call this straight after clicking a download link, instead of guessing that the file is ready.

folder.description: Folder the download lands in. Defaults to your output folder.

timeoutSeconds.description: Optional user-requested deadline. Omit to wait until complete or stopped.

nameContains.description: Only accept a file whose name contains this text.

linux.name: upload_file
linux.description: Attach a local file to a file-upload control on the current page, the same as choosing it in the file picker. Read the page first to get the id of the upload field.

ref.description: Element id of the file input, from browser_read.

path.description: Full path to the file to attach.

linux.name: get_datetime
linux.description: Get the current date and time. Pass an IANA time zone such as America/New_York or Europe/London to get the time in that place; omit it for this computer's local time.

linux.name: open_search_in_browser
linux.description: Open a Google search in the agent's own browser window for the user to look at. This does not return results to you; use web_search when you need the answer yourself.

linux.name: run_command
linux.description: Run a shell command with full local permissions in the requested working folder.

linux.name: open_url
linux.description: Open an HTTPS URL in the agent's own browser window (a separate profile, never the user's) for the user to see.

linux.name: open_page
linux.description: Open a web page in the agent's own browser window (a separate profile, never the user's) and bring it to the front, so you can then read it, click it, or type into it.

linux.name: browser_read
linux.description: Read the current web page as structured data: its text plus every clickable and typable element with a short id. This is the fast, exact way to see a page. Always prefer it over screenshots for anything in a browser.

linux.name: browser_text
linux.description: Read only the words on the current page, with no clickable element list. Use this when you just need to read an article, a result or a description and are not going to click anything, because it costs a fraction of what browser_read does on a long page.

maxCharacters.description: Stop after this many characters. Defaults to 40000.

linux.name: browser_screenshot
linux.description: Save a picture of the page currently open in the browser. Use this to show someone what a page looks like, or to check a layout. To read a page, use browser_text or browser_read instead — they are faster and exact.

path.description: Where to save it, ending in .png.

linux.name: browser_find
linux.description: Find elements on the current page whose text, label or placeholder contains a phrase. Returns their ids so you can click or fill them.

query.description: Words to look for, for example "Send" or "Search mail".

linux.name: browser_click
linux.description: Click an element on the page by the id browser_read gave it. Exact, no coordinates, no guessing.

linux.name: browser_fill
linux.description: Type an exact value into a text box, textarea or dropdown by its element id.

linux.name: browser_press
linux.description: Press a key such as Enter, Tab or Escape, optionally after focusing an element id.

key.description: Enter, Tab, Escape, ArrowDown, PageDown, and similar.

ref.description: Optional element id to focus first.

linux.name: browser_scroll
linux.description: Scroll the current page by a number of pixels. Positive scrolls down.

delta.description: Pixels to scroll, for example 800 or -800.

linux.name: browser_back
linux.description: Go back to the previous page in this browser tab.

linux.name: browser_wait_for
linux.description: Wait until a phrase appears on the page, for slow pages and apps that load after navigation.

linux.name: browser_tabs
linux.description: List the open browser tabs with their ids, titles and URLs.

linux.name: browser_open_tab
linux.description: Open one HTTPS page in a new browser tab and switch to it. Use this only for a small set of separate items that must be compared, such as the top 3–5 results from a ranked list.

url.description: The complete HTTPS URL to open.

linux.name: browser_switch_tab
linux.description: Switch to one of the open tabs by its id.

linux.name: browser_extensions
linux.description: List the browser extension windows that are currently open — a wallet asking to confirm, a VPN choosing a location, any extension popup — and the extensions installed in this browser. Call this when a task involves an extension, or when a page seems to be waiting on one.

linux.name: browser_focus_extension
linux.description: Switch to an open extension window so you can read and click inside it with the ordinary page tools. Use this to press Confirm, Approve, Sign, Connect or similar inside an extension. Switch back to the page afterwards with browser_switch_tab.

viewId.description: The viewId from browser_extensions. Omit it when only one extension window is open.

linux.name: browser_extract
linux.description: Pull a repeating list off the page as rows of data in one call: search results, table rows, product cards, listings. Give the CSS selector for one repeating item and a map of field name to selector. Add @href or @src to take an attribute instead of the text. Far faster than reading and scrolling.

rowSelector.description: CSS selector matching one repeating item, for example "article.listing" or "table tbody tr".

fields.description: Field name to selector within the row. Example: { "title": "h2", "price": ".price", "link": "a@href" }. Use "" to take the row text itself.

linux.name: browser_wait_for_idle
linux.description: Wait until the page has finished loading and its network traffic has gone quiet. Call this after navigating or clicking something slow, instead of reading the page over and over to see whether it is ready.

quietMillis.description: How long the network must stay quiet. Default 700.

timeoutSeconds.description: Optional user-requested deadline in seconds. Omit to wait until ready or stopped.

linux.name: browser_click_and_wait
linux.description: Click something and wait for what it was meant to cause, in one call: a new page, or some text appearing. Use this instead of clicking and then reading the page repeatedly to see whether it worked.

waitForText.description: Wait until this text appears on the page.

linux.name: browser_fill_form
linux.description: Fill several fields on the page in one call, then optionally press a button. Use this for a login or any form rather than filling one field per call.

fields.description: The fields to fill, in order.

submitRef.description: Element id of the button to click once the fields are filled.

linux.name: browser_evaluate
linux.description: Run a JavaScript expression inside the current page and get its value back. The fastest way to pull structured data out of a page: one call can return every row of a table or every listing on a results page as JSON, instead of reading and scrolling many times. The expression is evaluated in the page, so document, window and querySelectorAll are all available.

resultId.description: Temporary result ID returned by an earlier evaluation; set expression to an empty string when continuing.

offset.description: nextOffset returned by the previous result chunk.

expression.description: A JavaScript expression. Example: [...document.querySelectorAll("article")].map(a => ({ title: a.querySelector("h2")?.innerText, href: a.querySelector("a")?.href }))

linux.name: browser_console
linux.description: Read the browser console for the current page: script errors, warnings and log output. Use this when a page looks broken, half-loaded, or does not respond the way the page text suggests it should.

level.description: Use "error" for only errors and warnings.

limit.description: How many of the most recent messages to return. Default 50.

linux.name: browser_network
linux.description: List the network requests the current page made, with method, URL and status. Use it to find a blocked or failing request, or to spot the underlying data API a page calls, which is often quicker to read than the rendered page.

failedOnly.description: Only requests that failed or returned status 400 or above.

urlPattern.description: Only requests whose URL contains this text.

limit.description: How many of the most recent requests to return. Default 50.

linux.name: browser_hover
linux.description: Move the pointer onto an element without clicking, to open a hover menu or reveal a tooltip. Read the page afterwards to see what appeared.

linux.name: browser_click_special
linux.description: Click an element with the right mouse button, or double-click it. Use this for context menus and for lists where opening an item needs a double click. An ordinary single left click is browser_click.

clickCount.description: Use 2 for a double click. Default 1.

linux.name: browser_drag
linux.description: Drag one element onto another: reordering a list, moving a card between columns, or setting a slider.

fromRef.description: Element id to drag, from browser_read.

toRef.description: Element id to drop it onto, from browser_read.

linux.name: browser_resize
linux.description: Set the size of the page viewport, optionally emulating a mobile device. Useful for checking a mobile layout, and for making a page narrow enough that its content needs less scrolling.

mobile.description: Emulate a touch mobile device at that size.

linux.name: browser_close_tab
linux.description: Close one tab you opened, by its id. Use this to tidy up the extra tabs you opened before you give your final answer. Never close a tab that was already open before you started.

linux.name: read_screen
linux.description: Read the window that is in front — the open web page or app — and return its visible text and the buttons, links and fields you can act on. Call this before clicking or typing so you know what is really there.

linux.description: Click a button, link, checkbox or menu item in the window in front, found by the text you can see on it.

name.description: The visible text of the thing to click, copied from read_screen.

linux.description: Type text into the window in front. Pass into with a field name from read_screen to fill that field, or leave it out to type wherever the cursor already is.

into.description: The name or label of the field to type into.

linux.name: press_key
linux.description: Press one key in the window in front, such as Enter, Tab, Escape, PageDown, or a combination like Ctrl+S.

linux.name: scroll_page
linux.description: Scroll the window in front up or down to bring more content into view.

amount.description: How many notches to scroll. Defaults to 3.

linux.name: take_screenshot
linux.description: Save a PNG picture of the screen to a local file, so the user can see what is on it.

path.description: Where to save the .png file.

linux.name: check_screen

question.description: One thing to confirm, e.g. "does the calculator show 64".

linux.description: List the application windows that are open on this computer.

linux.name: focus_window

linux.name: open_app
linux.description: Start a Linux application, such as Text Editor, Calculator, or the full path to an executable.

name.description: The application to start, for example Text Editor.

path.description: Where to save it, including the file name and extension.

path.description: The output file, ending in .docx, .pdf or .xlsx.

content.description: For .docx and .pdf, the complete body text; start a line with # for a heading or - for a bullet. In a .pdf you can also place a picture you have already downloaded by putting its full path on its own line as ![](C: olderpicture.png) - use that to put each image beside the text about it.
